agent_vs_you: The agent's own plan was a single qwen image step; it ignored 'transparent PNG ... no white box' entirely and did not ask the image for a plain keyable ground. The code guard in plan.js then appended background-remove (the catalogue's TRANSPARENT rule and its 'WELL: a transparent PNG: a logo' line point there). That AI cutter is a salient-object segmenter: it kept the crescent and treated the word 'Mooncrumb' as background, deleting it. I would make the logo flat on pure white and key the white out by code (filter look: transparent, which exists in the harness but is not mentioned on filter's catalogue line), so every mark, including the lettering, is kept. The agent could not have chosen filter from what it saw: its line lists only bw/sepia/warm/cool/bright/dark/contrast.

your_plan.say: I'll design the Mooncrumb logo flat on plain white with the name lettered exactly, then turn the white into real transparency by code, so you get a PNG with nothing behind the moon and the name.

params.prompt_or_change: Flat vector bakery logo, centred: a solid gold (#C9A24A) crescent moon placed above the word "Mooncrumb" in dark navy (#14213D) elegant serif lettering. Flat solid colours only: no gradient, no shadow, no glow, no texture, no border, no frame, no other words. Isolated on a plain pure white (#FFFFFF) background with a generous empty margin all round.

steps.why: qwen letters the name exactly (it did here); a flat design on pure white is what a colour key can lift cleanly.

params.prompt_or_change: Make the plain white background transparent; keep the crescent and every letter exactly as they are.

steps.why: Code colour key of the border colour: keeps all navy and gold pixels, lettering included, and gives true alpha; the AI background remover erases text.

fix: 1) Catalogue: on filter add 'transparent: keys out the plain background of a flat design (logo, icon, sticker, lettering) into a true-alpha PNG, every mark kept'; on background-remove change WELL to 'a photographed product or person' and add CANNOT 'logos or designs with words: it erases the lettering'; change the CHOOSING rule to 'TRANSPARENT: a design made here -> image on plain pure white (say so in the prompt), then filter look: transparent; a photo subject -> background-remove'. 2) Keep the post-run plan.js guard that routes a lettered last step to filter, and extend it to any logo/icon/sticker/flat-vector image even without lettering, and have it append 'isolated on plain pure white, flat colours, no shadow' to that image prompt. 3) Grader: composite RGBA outputs over a checkerboard and a dark colour before sending them to the judge and report alpha coverage; it read alpha-0 pixels as a tan opaque square and would read a correctly keyed logo as a 'white box'.
evidence: mooncrumb-logo.png (qwen, 640x640) is a clean, correctly spelled logo: gold crescent above navy serif 'Mooncrumb' on near-white (250,250,250). mooncrumb-logo-transparent.png has alpha 0 on 397,979 of 409,600 pixels and every visible pixel lies in rows 160-360 (the crescent); the lettering rows (~370-450) are fully transparent, so background-remove erased the name. The RGB hidden under alpha 0 is gold (190,153,95), which is why the judge, whose input path drops alpha, described a 'tan square' with a 'faint crescent': the background really is transparent, but the fail is still right because the name is gone. Running the harness's own colorkey (0xfafafa:0.12:0.08) on mooncrumb-logo.png in memory keeps 23,097 opaque pixels including 8,468 in the lettering rows, with only 506 semi-transparent edge pixels.
